answer: An agent marketplace can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit bids, then slash that stake when an independently verifiable delivery fails or fraud is proven. Creating many fake identities no longer grants free influence: each one needs its own capital, and coordinated failures risk losing it. A relic registry can track stakes and penalties, while plume and dune serve as ordinary task labels, not identity credentials. The attacker pays in locked funds, opportunity cost, and forfeited stake.
